title: Expected closed-fibre equation count permits localization preserving reduction
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset R$ an ideal, $m,c\ge0$, and $S=R[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Here $m-c$ is the difference in $\mathbb Z$, so the following hypothesis requires $c\le m$ whenever there is a nonempty closed-reduction fibre. Assume every nonempty fibre of $S/IS$ over $R/I$ has Krull dimension $m-c$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Then there is $g\in S$ mapping to $1$ in $S/IS$ such that $S_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] has a presentation $R[y_1,\ldots,y_m,z]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c,hz-1)$, where $h$ maps to $g$, which is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Empty fibres, including $S/IS=0$, are allowed.

proof.text: If $S/IS=0$, choose $g=0$ and its polynomial lift $h=0$. Its image in the zero reduction is $1=0$. Inverting $0$ gives the zero ring, and the inverse-variable quotient has the relation $-1$, so is also zero. Every fibre is empty, and the relative global complete intersection condition is vacuous. Hence suppose $S/IS\ne0$. It has a maximal ideal, giving a prime of $S$ containing $IS$ and a nonempty fibre over its contraction in $R/I$. A nonempty spectrum has nonnegative dimension, so the hypothesis with the integer difference $m-c$ implies $c\le m$. Put $d=m-c\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 00ST (1); Tag 00SP (definition-relative-global-complete-intersection); Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), empty-spectrum and maximal-ideal cases

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\in V(IS)$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$, so $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. The quotient-spectrum correspondence identifies these with primes of $S/IS$ and $R/I$. The residue fields at $\mathfrak p/I$ and $\mathfrak p$ are identical: fractions modulo these primes have the same numerators and denominators. The fibre rings are canonically isomorphic: $(S/IS)\otimes_{R/I}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ sends $(s\bmod IS)\otimes a$ to $s\otimes a$, with inverse $s\otimes a\mapsto(s\bmod IS)\otimes a$; these are well defined since $I$ acts by zero on the field and inverse on pure tensors. Consequently the original fibre at $\mathfrak p$ has dimension $d$. Its point corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ has dimension some integer $e\le d$, since dimension at a point is the minimum of the dimensions of its open neighbourhoods and the whole fibre is one of them.

The images of the $m$ variables generate $S$ as an $R$-algebra, so $R\to S$ is of finite type. At each $\mathfrak q\in V(IS)$ apply the bounded-local-fibre-dimension neighbourhood theorem with the integer $e$ from step 2. It gives an open $V_{\mathfrak q}$ containing $\mathfrak q$ where every local fibre dimension is at most $e$, hence at most $d$. The union $W=\bigcup_{\mathfrak q\in V(IS)}V_{\mathfrak q}$ is open, contains $V(IS)$, and every point of $W$ has local fibre dimension at most $d$.

Write the closed complement of $W$ as $V(J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq S$, using the definition of the Zariski topology. Since $V(J)\cap V(IS)=\varnothing$, the disjoint-zero-loci criterion gives $g\in J$ and $u\in IS$ with $g+u=1$. Thus $g$ maps to $1$ in $S/IS$. If a prime does not contain $g$ it cannot contain $J$, so $D(g)\subseteq W$. Choose a polynomial preimage $h\in R[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ of $g$ under the surjective quotient map.

source.place: Tag 00ST (1), choice of J, g and h; Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology)

proof.text: Fix any prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and put $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\bar g=g\otimes1$. Localization base change identifies $S_g\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $F_{\bar g}$; its spectrum is the open $O=D(\bar g)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}F$. A point of $O$ corresponds by the fibre-prime bijection to a prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$ above $\mathfrak p$, and $\bar g\notin\mathfrak Q$ says exactly $g\notin\mathfrak q$. Thus $\mathfrak q\in D(g)\subseteq W$, and its local fibre dimension is at most $d$. Dimension at a point is unchanged on an open subspace, so every local dimension in $O$ is at most $d$. The dimension-supremum theorem now gives $\dim O\le d$, including $O=\varnothing$, whose dimension is $-\infty$. Hence every nonempty fibre of $S_g$ has dimension at most $d$.

source.place: Tag 00ST (1), passage from W to S_g; Tags 00DK/00DL, 00E4, 00E6; Topology Tag 0B7I (lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions)

proof.text: The inverse-variable presentation theorem identifies $S_g$ with $T=R[y_1,\ldots,y_m,z]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c,hz-1)$, sending the old variables to their localized images and $z$ to $1/g$. Base change of this presentation to any $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ presents $T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $m+1$ variables and $c+1$ equations. Since $c\le m$, the polynomial-quotient dimension lower bound applies to each nonzero such fibre and gives dimension at least $(m+1)-(c+1)=d$. The presentation isomorphism induces isomorphisms on fibre rings; their spectra are homeomorphic (the maps are mutually inverse on primes and on basic opens), hence have equal dimensions. Step 5 therefore supplies the upper bound $d$ for these same fibres. All nonempty fibres of the displayed presentation have dimension exactly $d$, so it is a relative global complete intersection by definition. The element $g$ retains the reduction established in step 4.

source.place: Tag 00ST (1), inverse-variable presentation and completion of the implicit dimension lower bound; Tag 05G3 (section-base-change); Tags 00OP and 00KW

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q106-e3159b2bf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 20 cited node statements and Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00ST (statement and the proofs of (1)-(3)). This is a first split with no new nodes and no re-split note. Statement: the only change from the base is one sentence saying m−c is the integer difference. That is already the convention of the cited def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection (its remark: c>n gives T=0), and truncated subtraction would make the statement false (R=k, m=0, c=1, f=0). 'Nonempty fibres' is weaker than the source's hypothesis, so the statement is not weakened, and the citer lem-sfb-syntomic-algebra-surjection-lift is unaffected. Steps: (1) S/IS=0 with g=h=0 makes everything vacuous; otherwise a maximal ideal gives a nonempty fibre, so c≤m. (2) The fibre rings over R/I and R are matched by an explicit tensor isomorphism (I acts as 0 on κ(p)), and the local dimension e≤d follows from the definition as a minimum. (3) 00QH node with that integer e gives an open W⊇V(IS) where every local fibre dimension is ≤d. (4) Disjoint zero loci give g∈J with g≡1 mod IS, and D(g)⊆W. (5) Localization base change, the D(g) homeomorphism, the fibre-prime bijection (same point ker ψ_q), invariance of local dimension on an open subspace and the 0B7I supremum give fibres of S_g of dimension ≤d. (6) The inverse-variable presentation, presentation base change, and the polynomial-quotient lower bound (m+1≥c+1, nonzero fibre) give dimension exactly d, so the presentation is a relative global complete intersection. Small cases: R=k[t], I=(t), f1=y1(1−ty2), f2=y2(1−ty2), where the generic fibre jumps to dimension 1 and g=1−ty2 removes the line; also I=0 and m=c=0. No duplicate: the existing 00ST nodes all state assertion (3). Accepted tool_uses: the sk-thm-p1 generic lemmas (00QH bound, open-subspace local dimension, 0B7I supremum, localize-presentation, polynomial lower bound). The null blueprint.from.node is inherited from the base. No SGA. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_localization_relativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_preserving_reduction (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (m c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin m) R) (hdim : IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersectionPresentation (fun i ↦ MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (f i))) : ∃ h : MvPolynomial (Fin m) R, Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap R (MvPolynomial (Fin m) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)))) (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) h) = 1 ∧ IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersectionPresentation (Fin.snoc (α := fun _ ↦ MvPolynomial (Fin (m + 1)) R) (fun i ↦ MvPolynomial.rename Fin.castSucc (f i)) (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.castSucc h * MvPolynomial.X (Fin.last m) - 1)) ∧ ∃ e : (MvPolynomial (Fin (m + 1)) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (Fin.snoc (α := fun _ ↦ MvPolynomial (Fin (m + 1)) R) (fun i ↦ MvPolynomial.rename Fin.castSucc (f i)) (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.castSucc h * MvPolynomial.X (Fin.last m) - 1)))) ≃ₐ[R] Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) h), (∀ i : Fin m, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X (Fin.castSucc i))) = algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) h)) (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X i))) ∧ e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X (Fin.last m))) = IsLocalization.Away.invSelf (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) h)
